ledger.note: Later in 2018: 'the group took parts of Lahij and Dhale'. The page gives no month and no extent; only the Lahij disc is drawn.

28 January 2018: the STC seizes government headquarters in Aden. 'STC-loyal forces seized the Yemeni government headquarters in Aden'; the council had been formed in Aden on 11 May 2017 with UAE support and President Hadi called it 'illegitimate'. The Yemen page used by republic-of-yemen says February 2018.

27-29 August 2019: the fighting for Aden. 'UAE-backed Security Belt forces lost territory to Hadi-aligned troops, who advanced on Aden'; on 29 August UAE airstrikes killed or injured over 300 government soldiers. The page does not give a date for the STC taking Aden.
5 November 2019: the Riyadh Agreement. 'The government recognized the STC, and the STC withdrew militarily from Aden and gave up some southern security control.'

5 November 2019: the STC withdraws militarily from Aden under the Riyadh Agreement. The page does not say how much of Aden's administration it kept; the government returns in name only (the STC reoccupied its institutions on 26 April 2020).
2020: Socotra. 'The STC took over Socotra Governorate' (no month or counterpart on the page).

26 April 2020: self-governance declared and Aden's institutions occupied. 'The STC declared self-governance' and 'occupied Aden's government institutions'; the government called it 'a clear and definite coup'. The local authorities of Hadramaut, Abyan, Shabwa, Al-Mahrah and Socotra rejected the move.

August 2022: Abyan and Shabwah. The STC 'launched an offensive in Abyan and Shabwah, capturing most of their districts'; the war page: 'launches an offensive against the Islah party, taking large amounts of territory (August 2022)'. The STC had joined the Presidential Leadership Council in April 2022 with al-Zoubaidi as vice president.

region.text: Hadramawt, Al Mahrah and the rest of former South Yemen

ledger.note: 2-9 December 2025: Operation Promising Future. The STC launched a large-scale offensive in Hadramaut on 2 December; by 8 December it held most of the six (the war page: eight) former South Yemen governorates, 'including Hadramawt and Al-Mahrah'; PLC chair al-Alimi and the prime minister left Aden for Riyadh.

2-4 January 2026: Hadramawt and Al Mahrah retaken. 'PLC-aligned forces, backed by Saudi forces and the Hadramaut Tribal Alliance, retook Hadramawt and Al-Mahrah'; government forces captured Seiyun on 3 January and Mukalla on 4 January (war page).
6-7 January 2026: Abyan and Shabwah. 'After Saudi airstrikes, PLC-aligned forces pushed the STC out of Abyan and Shabwah.'

7 January 2026: Aden. Government forces began entering Aden; al-Zoubaidi left for Berbera and then the UAE and 'the STC lost its capital'. Lahij, Dhale and Socotra are folded in as the researcher's reading: the pages do not name them.

9 January 2026: dissolution announced. STC members, in a Riyadh statement, announced the council's dissolution, saying the offensive 'harmed the southern cause'; the UAE-based spokesman Anwar al-Tamimi called the news 'ridiculous', and officials later called the statement 'null and void' and made under duress. The council had published a constitutional declaration for a 'State of South Arabia' on 2 January 2026.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (its Yemen rows draw the whole country; republic-of-yemen's 2018-02 contest_start names this slug). Written by me-10-x; 2 pages opened (budget up to 5), no more. Pages differ on the day and month of the Aden takeover (28 January 2018 on the STC page; February 2018 on the war page) and on the number of governorates held in December 2025 (six; eight). The council is typed rebel because no state recognised it, although it sat in the Presidential Leadership Council from April 2022. It held ten or more years only if its 2017 formation is counted; the land counted here is eight years (January 2018 to January 2026). The Lahij part carried through 2024 and the loss of Lahij, Dhale and Socotra in January 2026 are the researcher's reading (the pages give no event for them). Not opened: the 2018 and 2019 battles of Aden, the Riyadh Agreement, the Socotra takeover and the Hadramaut offensive articles. Counterpart for the Presidential Leadership Council is republic-of-yemen, the only state dossier; the PLC dossier does not exist. Dissolution is disputed on the page itself.
